full_judgment:
8. Now I pass over to consider the question of limitation urged by the learned Advocate for the opposite party in the instant case in filing the application for revision. The learned Advocate referred to Sub-Section 2(b) of Section 29 of the Limitation Act which speaks that the remaining provision of this Act shall not apply and thereby the learned Advocate for the opposite party argued that Section 5 of Limitation Act having no application in view of Section 29(b) of Limitation Act, the revisional application must be held to be barred by time as it was filed five months several days after the passing of impugned order. In this connection the learned Advocate for opposite party has cited a decision in the case of Govt. of People's Republic of Bangladesh Vs. Kobad Ali and others, reported in 1987 B.L.D. (A.D.) page 268. The controversy that cropped up in the cited case was whether article 181 of Limitation Act will apply or not. Their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that the Court's power to revise and order suo-motu is not restricted by time limit. But revisional application is to be filed within a period of 90 days. The High Court Division may in its discretion be able to entertain an application beyond that period if there is no negligence or laches on the part of the petitioner. In the instant case, 5 Months 7 days delay occurred and at the time of issuing the Rule, the delay was condoned. At para 4 of the application, the delay has been explained and the Court being satisfied with the explanation offered for condonation of delay, condoned the delay. Their Lordships of the Appellate Division made observation in following language: 

 9. In the instant case, no laches was committed by the petitioner inasmuch as the main tadbirkar fell ill. So, in view of the decision of the Appellate Division referred above, the application for revision is not hit by Section 2(b) or Section 29 of Limitation Act which has no manner of application in the instant case.
